title: Bone scan
what: A small dose of a tracer substance is injected into a vein. It collects in the bones, and a special camera takes images of the whole skeleton.
why: To find changes in the bones when the doctor needs to see the whole skeleton at once, or for bone pain with no clear cause.
duration: the whole visit usually takes 3 to 5 hours: the injection, 2 to 4 hours of waiting, and a 20 to 40 minute scan; the report in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: If you are or might be pregnant
If you are breastfeeding. You will need a break
If you recently had other tests with tracers or barium
If it is hard to lie on your back for 30 minutes

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no special prep. You can eat and drink.

prepare.title: Water
prepare.text: After the injection, you are asked to drink plenty of water and use the toilet often.

prepare.title: Metal
prepare.text: Before the scan, take off jewelry and your belt, and empty your pockets of keys.

bring: Water and something to read while you wait
steps: You get an injection into a vein, just like a blood test
You wait 2 to 4 hours, drink water, and use the toilet
Before the scan, you empty your bladder
You lie on your back, and the camera moves slowly over your body
You lie still for 20 to 40 minutes
feel: The injection feels like giving blood
You do not feel the tracer at all
The camera is close, but it does not touch you or make noise
after: That day, drink more water and use the toilet more often
For about 24 hours, it is usually best not to hold small children or sit close to pregnant women. Check with the clinic
Take the report to the doctor who referred you

faq.a: The dose is small, about the same as a CT scan. The tracer leaves your body quickly in your urine.

faq.q: Can I be around children after the scan?
faq.a: You are usually advised not to hold babies for 24 hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

reminders.text: Bone scan tomorrow. The visit takes 3 to 5 hours. Bring water and something to read.
